_about: Single source of truth for every Caution (yellow) / Critical (red) limit. Values are copied only from the team's spec documents (internal, written in Turkish, not published in this repository). Never edit a medical value here without a spec document change. Screens must not hard-code any of these numbers.

general.source: Main Panel Alarm Checklist, 'five rules that apply to every alarm' 1-2: yellow needs 24 h average or 3 consecutive readings out of range; red is verified with a second reading within 5 min unless the person feels unwell.

bp_systolic.label: Blood pressure (systolic)
bp_systolic.source: Main Panel Alarm Checklist: high yellow 130/80 or above, red upper >180; low yellow upper <=100, red upper <=90. Orthostatic drop (upper -20 / lower -10 on standing) is also red; needs a stand test, not evaluated from a single reading.
bp_systolic.explain: Blood pressure is the force of blood on the vessel walls; the first number is the upper (systolic) value. In space it reads 8–10 units lower than on Earth, so high values are taken more seriously here.

bp_diastolic.label: Blood pressure (diastolic)
bp_diastolic.source: Main Panel Alarm Checklist: high yellow 130/80 or above, red lower >120.
bp_diastolic.explain: The second blood pressure number is the lower (diastolic) value, measured between heartbeats.

hrv.label: HRV (rMSSD)
openItems: Checklist says red is 'below 15-19 ms'; 15 is used because it is red under either reading. Team must confirm the exact value.
Red rule 'far below personal normal for 3 days in a row' is not quantified in the documents; not implemented.
hrv.source: Main Panel Alarm Checklist (HRV); normal band = personal baseline mean +/- 0.5 SD (SWC), 7-day average, at least 3 valid readings per week (Chart Blueprint, 'middle panel limits').
hrv.explain: HRV shows how flexibly the time between heartbeats changes. It is a sign of fatigue, stress and recovery, and is compared with your own normal, not with other people.

spo2.label: SpO₂
spo2.source: Main Panel Alarm Checklist: yellow <=94 % or sudden 3-point drop; red <=91 % (<=85 % very urgent). Normal 94-98 %.
spo2.explain: The finger sensor shows the share of oxygen in the blood. The normal range is 94–98 %. If more than one person drops, the problem is the cabin air, not the person.

body_temp.label: Body temperature
body_temp.source: Main Panel Alarm Checklist: high yellow >=38.5 °C resting; red >=39.1 °C resting or >=40.0 °C any time; low yellow <=36.0 °C, red <=35.0 °C.
body_temp.explain: On long missions resting body temperature settles near 38 °C, so the 38 °C fever limit used on Earth does not apply here.

radiation_rate.label: Radiation (current)
radiation_rate.source: Main Panel Alarm Checklist: yellow >1.3 mSv/day (deep space) or >0.8 mSv/day (surface); red when a solar event starts or a single event reaches 50 mSv.

radiation_event_dose.label: Radiation (event dose)
radiation_event_dose.source: Main Panel Alarm Checklist: single event >=50 mSv is red (shelter threshold proposed by the draft; event limit 250 mSv).

radiation_cumulative.label: Radiation (cumulative)
radiation_cumulative.source: Main Panel Alarm Checklist: cumulative yellow >=480 mSv, red 600 mSv (career limit).

cabin_co2.label: Cabin CO₂
cabin_co2.source: Single Story Plan 'threshold decision' + Chart Blueprint panel C (NASA OCHMO-TB-004): yellow >=2.5, red 1-h average >3.0 mmHg; 4.0 mmHg stays as the emergency level.

cabin_pio2.label: Cabin O₂ (inspired, PIO₂)
cabin_pio2.source: Chart Blueprint panel B (NASA-STD-3001 Vol 2, Table 6.2-1): normal 145-155 mmHg, yellow 127-144 (proposal), red below 127. PIO₂ = (cabin pressure - 47) x O₂ fraction. No upper limit is given in the documents.

cabin_pressure.label: Cabin pressure
cabin_pressure.source: Team build guide (drafted with AI assistance), Table A: normal 14.4-14.9 psia, yellow 14.0-14.39, red <14.0.

cabin_temp.label: Cabin temperature
openItems: Red is defined only as 'life-support system failure' with no numeric value; no red threshold is configured.
cabin_temp.source: Main Panel Alarm Checklist + team build guide, Table A: suitable range 20-25 °C; outside range is yellow.

eva_margin.label: Return margin
eva_margin.source: EVA Panel v2, M1: Caution margin <60 min; Critical margin <=30 min (EMU backup life support = 30 min).

action.critical: Start the return now. Take no new task.

eva_suit_pressure.label: Suit pressure
openItems: Thresholds are computed for the EMU (4.3 psi, 100 % O₂); suit type is not confirmed.
eva_suit_pressure.source: EVA Panel v2, M4: silent Caution <4.05 psi; Critical <3.8 psi; absolute lower limit 3.36 psi.

action.critical: End the EVA, switch to backup O₂, return. Check for decompression symptoms.

eva_pico2.label: Inspired CO₂ (PICO₂)
openItems: NASA-STD-3001 Table 11.3-1 numeric limits could not be accessed; the Caution threshold must be compared with that table.
eva_pico2.source: EVA Panel v2, M5: silent Caution >8 mmHg for 15 min; Critical >15 mmHg; absolute limit 20 mmHg for at most 1 h.

action.critical: End the EVA and return. Check for headache, shortness of breath, confusion.

eva_metabolic_rate.label: Metabolic rate
eva_metabolic_rate.source: EVA Panel v2, M6: Caution 15-min average >1200 BTU/h; Critical >2100 BTU/h for 5 min.

action.caution: Take a rest break, slow down, increase cooling.
action.critical: Stop the activity. If values do not fall at rest, end the EVA.

eva_heart_rate.label: Heart rate
eva_heart_rate.source: EVA Panel v2, M6: Caution HR >140; Critical HR >90 % personal HRmax (measured, else 208 - 0.7 x age). Critical also on mismatch: HR >140 while primary-source metabolic rate <1000 BTU/h.

action.caution: Take a rest break, slow down, increase cooling.
action.critical: Stop the activity. If values do not fall at rest, end the EVA.

eva_orthostatic_hr_rise.label: Orthostatic HR rise (upright, low effort, 10 min)
eva_orthostatic_hr_rise.source: EVA Panel v2, M8: Caution HR rise >=30 within 10 min upright at low effort or mild symptom; Critical on pre-syncope symptom or systolic drop >=20 / diastolic >=10 mmHg (symptom-driven, wired in Step 3).

action.caution: Slow down, drink water, rest 5 min.

eva_o2.label: O₂ / backup O₂

caution.label: backup O₂ not full before EVA
O₂ use 20 % above metabolic expectation – leak suspected

eva_o2.source: EVA Panel v2, M2: Caution backup O₂ not full before EVA, or O₂ use 20 % above metabolic expectation for 10 min while pressure falls (leak suspicion, proposal); Critical backup O₂ engaged for any reason.

action.caution: Partner: visual leak check. Time budget recalculated.
action.critical: Start the return now. Keep a controlled pace: cooling is reduced on backup O₂.

eva_return_by.label: Return by
eva_return_by.source: EVA Panel v2, M1: Critical when return-by time D <= 0 (D keeps the return consumption and the 30-min reserve aside).

eva_suit_time.label: Total suit time
eva_suit_time.source: EVA Panel v2, M1: Caution total suit time >= 12 h (proposal).

eva_suit_time_with_return.label: Suit time incl. return
eva_suit_time_with_return.source: EVA Panel v2, M1 / NASA-STD-3001: total time in suit must not exceed 14 h including the return.

eva_drink_rate.label: Drinking water intake
eva_drink_rate.source: EVA Panel v2, M3: Caution when drinking <240 mL/h (2-h average, proposal). Never Critical on its own.

eva_drink_bag.label: Drink bag
eva_drink_bag.source: EVA Panel v2, M3: Caution when the bag is below 20 % (proposal).

eva_pico2_excess.label: Inspired CO₂ above expected
eva_pico2_excess.source: EVA Panel v2, M5: measured PICO₂ more than 3 mmHg above the value expected from metabolic rate (Kim et al. 2020 curve) -> silent Caution (proposal).

eva_core_rise.label: Core temperature rise since EVA start
eva_core_rise.source: EVA Panel v2, M7: Caution core temperature +0.6 °C above the EVA-start reference (first 10 min average).

action.caution: Increase cooling, slow down, drink water.

eva_skin_rise.label: Skin temperature rise since EVA start
eva_skin_rise.source: EVA Panel v2, M7: Caution skin temperature +1.4 °C above the EVA-start reference.

action.caution: Increase cooling, slow down, drink water.

eva_core_temp.label: Core temperature
eva_core_temp.source: EVA Panel v2, M7: Critical core >= 39.5 °C (proposal) or cooling off; >= 40.0 °C opens the overheating emergency instruction.

action.critical: Stop the activity, set cooling to maximum, start the return.

eva_ori.label: Orthostatic risk (ORI)
eva_ori.source: EVA Panel v2, M8 (surface EVA only): Caution ORI >= 60 or mild symptom; Critical ORI >= 80 or pre-syncope symptom. ORI from the G-TRANSIT v1.1 suit mode.

action.caution: Slow down, drink water, rest 5 min.
action.critical: Sit or lie down now. Partner comes to you. Consider ending the EVA.

eva_radiation.label: Radiation (suit dosimeter)
eva_radiation.source: EVA Panel v2, M9: Caution solar proton warning; Critical solar event started or suit dosimeter dose rate red.

action.caution: Task list shortened. Check the time to shelter.
action.critical: End the EVA and return to shelter.

eva_partner_voice_loss.label: No voice contact with partner

critical.label: partner does not answer two calls

eva_partner_voice_loss.source: EVA Panel v2, M9: Caution no voice with partner >2 min (proposal); Critical partner does not answer two calls.

action.caution: Get eye contact with your partner; use hand signals.
action.critical: Go to your partner. Check their pressure, O₂ and heart rate.

eva_habitat_link_loss.label: No habitat link
eva_habitat_link_loss.source: EVA Panel v2, M9: Caution no habitat link >10 min (proposal).

radiation_measured.label: Radiation dose rate (measured)
radiation_measured.source: Real data: NASA OSDR RadLab, ISS DOSTEL-1 absorbed dose rate, replayed. No limit is configured: the documents give radiation limits in mSv (dose equivalent), not in absorbed dose rate, and no conversion factor.

lab_hemoglobin.label: Hemoglobin
lab_hemoglobin.source: Periodic Health Tasks Checklist, section 2 (blood and urine tests), 'Limit values' table: normal male >=13, female >=12 g/dL; yellow male 11–12.9, female 11–11.9; red <11; <=7 very urgent. Sources in the document: WHO 2024, UCSF.

lab_sodium.label: Sodium
lab_sodium.source: Periodic Health Tasks Checklist, section 2 (blood and urine tests), 'Limit values' table: normal 135–145; yellow 120–134 or 146–160; red <120 or >160 mmol/L.

lab_potassium.label: Potassium
lab_potassium.source: Periodic Health Tasks Checklist, section 2 (blood and urine tests), 'Limit values' table: normal 3.5–5.2; yellow 2.8–3.4 or 5.3–6.2; red <2.8 or >6.2 mmol/L.

lab_ionized_calcium.label: Ionized calcium
openItems: Yellow is 'outside the device normal range'; the device range is not given in the documents, so only the red limits are evaluated.
lab_ionized_calcium.source: Periodic Health Tasks Checklist, section 2 (blood and urine tests), 'Limit values' table: normal = the device's normal range; yellow outside it; red <0.80 or >1.55 mmol/L.

lab_crp.label: CRP (inflammation)
lab_crp.source: Periodic Health Tasks Checklist, section 2 (blood and urine tests), 'Limit values' table: normal <5 mg/L; yellow 10–100 (5–10: repeat after 1 week); red >100 mg/L.

lab_urine_sg.label: Urine specific gravity
openItems: 'Below 1.005 and continuing' needs a rule for 'continuing'; a single low reading is shown as yellow.
lab_urine_sg.source: Periodic Health Tasks Checklist, section 2 (blood and urine tests), 'Limit values' table: normal 1.005–1.030; yellow >1.030, or <1.005 and continuing; red >1.035. Measured weekly, first morning urine.

lab_hematocrit.label: Hematocrit
lab_hematocrit.source: Periodic Health Tasks Checklist, section 2 (blood and urine tests), 'Limit values' table: normal male 39–52 %, female 36–48 %; yellow male 33–38.9, female 33–35.9, or above 52 / 48 (proposal); red <33 %; <=21 % very urgent.

lab_glucose.label: Glucose (fasting)
lab_glucose.source: Periodic Health Tasks Checklist, section 2 (blood and urine tests), 'Limit values' table: normal 70–105; yellow 56–69 or 106–400 (proposal); red <55 or >400 mg/dL.

lab_bun.label: Urea nitrogen (BUN)
lab_bun.source: Periodic Health Tasks Checklist, section 2 (blood and urine tests), 'Limit values' table: normal 7–20; yellow 21–65 (proposal); red >65 mg/dL.

lab_creatinine.label: Creatinine
openItems: The +30 % from personal baseline rule needs a preflight baseline; not evaluated yet.
lab_creatinine.source: Periodic Health Tasks Checklist, section 2 (blood and urine tests), 'Limit values' table (continued): normal 0.6–1.2; yellow 1.3–5.0 or a rise of more than 30 % from the person's own baseline (proposal); red >5.0 mg/dL.

lab_chloride.label: Chloride
lab_chloride.source: Periodic Health Tasks Checklist, section 2 (blood and urine tests), 'Limit values' table (continued): normal 98–107; yellow 80–97 or 108–120 (proposal); red <80 or >120 mmol/L.

lab_total_co2.label: Total CO₂ (bicarbonate)
lab_total_co2.source: Periodic Health Tasks Checklist, section 2 (blood and urine tests), 'Limit values' table (continued): normal 23–29; yellow 10–22 or 30–40 (proposal); red <10 or >40 mmol/L.

sleep_hours.label: Sleep

critical.label: 3 nights in a row below 5 h (proposal)

sleep_hours.source: Periodic Health Tasks Checklist (15 Nov 2026), section 11: normal 7-day average 6 h or more; yellow below 6 h; red 3 nights in a row below 5 h or below 5 h the night before a critical task (proposals; the critical-task part is the readiness red gate).

cognition_z.label: Cognitive test
cognition_z.source: Chart Blueprint, Mission readiness panel: cognitive test z-score against the person's own baseline, every 2–3 weeks.

reaction_ms.label: Reaction time
reaction_ms.source: Periodic Health Tasks Checklist (15 Nov 2026), section 3: short sleep, stress and cabin CO₂ slow reaction time; yellow = clearly slower than the person's own normal in 2 tests in a row. The numeric size of 'clearly' is set by the flight surgeon (open item), so no colour limit here. Test: median of 5 visual reactions on this panel.
openItems: How much slower than the own normal counts as 'clearly' (flight surgeon)

rad_daily_dose.label: Daily effective dose (estimate)
rad_daily_dose.source: Astronaut Radiation Monitoring: effects, measurement, sensors, data sources, dose calculation and limits (14 Nov 2026): E_day ≈ Σ t_k·Ḣ_k + E_EVA (time-weighted area monitor dose rate, EVA counted apart). Limits are applied as ratios by core/radiation.ts.

rad_eva_dose.label: EVA extra dose, skin and eye (estimate)
rad_eva_dose.source: Astronaut Radiation Monitoring: effects, measurement, sensors, data sources, dose calculation and limits (14 Nov 2026): E_day ≈ Σ t_k·Ḣ_k + E_EVA (time-weighted area monitor dose rate, EVA counted apart). Limits are applied as ratios by core/radiation.ts.

eye_vision_lines.label: Vision test, lines lost
eye_vision_lines.source: Periodic Health Tasks Checklist (15 Nov 2026), section 1: 1 line lost yellow, 2 or more lines or sudden loss red (proposals). Monthly computer vision test.

eye_iop.label: Intraocular pressure
eye_iop.source: Periodic Health Tasks Checklist (15 Nov 2026), section 1: normal 10–21, yellow 22–30 (above 21 on at least 2 readings), red above 30 (proposal), above 40 fast vision loss. Measured only on complaint.

nutrition_kcal_pct.label: Energy intake, % of plan
nutrition_kcal_pct.source: Periodic Health Tasks Checklist (15 Nov 2026), section 4: normal 90 % of plan or more; yellow 3 days in a row below 80 %; red 7 days in a row below 70 % or no eating (proposals).

water_l.label: Water intake

caution.label: 2 days in a row below 2.5 L (proposal)

water_l.source: Periodic Health Tasks Checklist (15 Nov 2026), section 4: normal 2.5 L/day or more; yellow 2 days in a row below 2.5 L; red below 1.5 L or no urine for 12 h (proposals).

sleep_med_nights.label: Sleep medication
sleep_med_nights.source: Periodic Health Tasks Checklist (15 Nov 2026), section 5: yellow sleep medication 3 or more nights a week (proposal). Red items (allergic reaction, wrong dose) are events, not numbers.

ecg_max_pause.label: ECG longest pause
ecg_max_pause.source: Periodic Health Tasks Checklist (15 Nov 2026), section 7: pause 2–3 s without symptoms yellow (proposal); longer than 3 s red (Holter syncope criteria).

body_mass_loss.label: Body mass loss vs preflight
body_mass_loss.source: Periodic Health Tasks Checklist (15 Nov 2026), section 8: below 5 % normal (3–4 % expected in the first 30 days); yellow 5 % or more (proposal); red 10 % or more.

fitness_pct.label: Aerobic fitness vs preflight
fitness_pct.source: Periodic Health Tasks Checklist (15 Nov 2026), section 9: normal 85 % of preflight or more; yellow below 85 % (proposal); red below 80 %.

fitness_vo2peak.label: VO2peak
fitness_vo2peak.source: Periodic Health Tasks Checklist (15 Nov 2026), section 9: red below 32.9 mL/kg/min before a spacewalk (source in the checklist).

strength_pct.label: Muscle strength vs baseline
strength_pct.source: Periodic Health Tasks Checklist (15 Nov 2026), section 10: normal 90 % of baseline or more; yellow below 90 % (proposal); red below 80 %. ARED strength test.

bone_urine_ca.label: 24-h urine calcium
bone_urine_ca.source: Bone Loss document (14 Nov 2026): 24-h urine calcium against the personal preflight baseline; levels from R_Ca in core/musculo.ts.

bone_ntx.label: Urine NTX
bone_ntx.source: Bone Loss document: urine N-telopeptide (resorption), personal baseline; plateau about +113 % (meta-analysis PMC7200725).

bone_bsap.label: BSAP (formation)
bone_bsap.source: Bone Loss document: bone-specific alkaline phosphatase; unchanged for 30 days, then about +7 % a month (PMC7200725).

muscle_leg_press.label: Leg press strength
muscle_leg_press.source: Exercise Program document (15 Nov 2026): loss % = (1 − P/P0) × 100 against preflight P0.

muscle_knee_torque.label: Knee extension peak torque
muscle_knee_torque.source: Exercise Program document: isokinetic knee extension, e.g. 191 → 188 Nm Sprint, 208 → 195 Nm standard (English et al. 2020).

ared_volume.label: ARED volume load
ared_volume.source: Exercise Program document: volume load = sets × reps × load, recorded by ARED.

goes_proton_flux.label: Solar protons ≥10 MeV (GOES)
goes_proton_flux.source: NOAA SWPC GOES integral protons (real, replayed). NOAA S-scale S1 10, S2 100, S3 1000, S4 10 000, S5 100 000 pfu; environment indicator, not astronaut dose (radiation document). S2 or above is a Warning in the radiation ledger.

eva._about: EVA calculation constants from EVA Panel v2 (eva_config.yaml section). Values marked proposal there need flight-surgeon approval.

symptomDiary.source: Periodic Health Tasks Checklist, section 6 (symptom diary), all values marked as proposal: yellow = same complaint 3 days in a row or severity 4–6 of 10; red = severity 7 or more, or a red-flag complaint (list in checkin.json)

readiness.source: Chart Blueprint (Crew Oxygen Chart and Mission Readiness Panel), section 5. All weights, windows and score bands are marked as proposals, to be approved by the flight surgeon.

crewOxygen.source: Chart Blueprint, section 3 'Environment or person: decision rule' (10 min window, 3-point drop, 24 h median are proposals) and Main Panel Alarm Checklist (SpO₂ <=94 %).

hexagon.source: Health Hexagon: data sources, download instructions and references (14 Nov 2026), 'Thresholds and normalisation' table; axis list from the team hexagon table. Axes 0 = no load, 1 = full load; ring at 0.6 = ORI 60. The polygon raises no alarm. No number here means 'hexagon validated'.

axes.label: Autonomic reserve
axes.basis: Personal baseline, no population norm (Nunan et al. 2010); baseline from ≥5 min rest (Task Force 1996). Needs effort correction (Lewis et al. 2007).
axes.status: sourced principle; limit to be set from data

axes.label: Heart-rate deviation
axes.basis: Postural tachycardia ≥30 bpm (Freeman 2011, same as M8). β₁ must be personal: NASA EVA HR–MR model R² 0.402 pooled, >0.82 per person (NTRS 20210024317).

axes.label: Vasodilation
axes.basis: G-TRANSIT V grad_hi / grad_lo (heuristic in the Blueprint); ΔTre−Tsk with HR reaches AUC 0.88 (CDC Stacks 210476).
axes.status: heuristic; to calibrate with Mendeley sets

axes.label: Heat storage
axes.basis: Temperature term of the PSI, Moran et al. 1998; risk PSI 7.5 (Buller 2008); ACGIH core limit 38.5 °C. No validated limit for the time integral, so the PSI term is drawn.
axes.status: PSI term sourced; integral from data

axes.label: Volume deficit
axes.basis: In-flight plasma loss 10–15 % (Fortney et al. 2001); 20 % in presyncopal landing crew vs 7 % (Waters et al. 2002); Montain & Coyle 1992.

axes.label: Cumulative effort
axes.basis: No physiological limit. NASA metabolic classes low ≤700, moderate 700–1000, high ≥1000 BTU/h; highest measured 1747 BTU/h (NTRS 20220009964). Apollo EVA means 780–1200 BTU/h (NASA TN D-7883).
axes.status: classes sourced; scale is a design decision

radiation.source: Astronaut Radiation Monitoring: effects, measurement, sensors, data sources, dose calculation and limits (14 Nov 2026). Limits: career 600 mSv effective (NASA-STD-3001 Vol 1 [V1 4030]); SPE 250 mSv per event [V1 4031]; 30-day organ limits blood-forming organs 250, lens 1000, skin 1500 mGy-Eq and yearly 500 / 2000 / 3000 (NCRP 132, NASA 30-day PEL). Free-space GCR about 0.5 mSv/day. Operational steps 0.5 / 0.8 / 1.0 of a limit and 3x the normal dose rate are the document's design choice (ALARA), not NASA's.

bone.source: Bone Loss document, 14 Nov 2026. Method 2: R_Ca = (U − U0)/U0; ΔCa ≈ −250 mg/day × min(R_Ca, 1); monthly loss % ≈ 30·|ΔCa| / skeletal Ca × 100. Skeletal calcium 1100 g is from memory in the document (not verified). Steps 0.5 / 1 / 1.5 are the document's design choice.

muscle.source: Astronaut Exercise Program document, 15 Nov 2026: R_kas = min(loss % / 20, 1) (20 % = NASA muscle concern level, English et al. 2020); compliance U = completed / planned volume load over 7 days. Bands 0.25 / 0.5 and U 0.6 / 0.85 are the team's proposal.

baseline._about: Personal Baseline and Sex Differences (team document, 15 Nov 2026). Robust z = (x − baseline median) / max(1.4826 · MAD, σ_floor). The baseline only adds an early warning (yellow, or 'orange' = yellow that asks the person to confirm); it never turns a red into yellow and never makes red. Final colour = the worse of the baseline colour and the absolute-limit colour. All numbers are the team's proposals, not NASA standards, not validated on astronaut data. Verified 15 Nov 2026 (team source-verification notes): Norsk 2015 (PMC4324706, ISS 85–192 days, 8 men) found 24 h systolic / diastolic / mean pressure 8 / 9 / 10 mmHg lower than preflight ambulatory values, nightly dip 8 ± 3 mmHg kept, heart rate unchanged — an Earth seated reference would flag everyone, hence supine and the flight baseline.
openItems: σ_floor per parameter (document: set by the team; not given) – until then σ_floor = 0

Width of the temporary wide band in the first 2 weeks of flight (document gives none; its basis is Fritsch-Yelle 1996, Shuttle, 12 astronauts: diastolic −5 mmHg, as reported in Norsk 2015) – until then the baseline colour is not used in the first 14 flight days
x = median of the last 60 min of readings (implementation choice, same idea as 'one reading is not an alarm')
baseline.source: Personal Baseline and Sex Differences: design, data and references for the astronaut health monitor (Spark team, 15 Nov 2026), sections 'Colour code against the personal baseline' and 'Sex-specific rules on the panel'.

sexRules._about: Sex is a risk modifier, not a correction (NTRS 20040088708: within-sex differences are as large as between-sex). Used only in the documented rules; never to change a normal range. Verified against PMC4236030 and the NTRS 20040088708 abstract (15 Nov 2026).

landingOrthostatic.rule: Landing and first 72 h: a standing-baseline deviation is shown as a visible caution with 'Sit down first' (others: logged quietly). Same threshold, more frequent warning.
landingOrthostatic.source: NTRS 20040088708 (abstract) and PMC4236030: presyncope after landing more frequent in women; the only sex difference with enough data

urinaryFirst.rule: Urinary symptoms (burning or frequent urination) are asked first in the symptom diary.
urinaryFirst.source: PMC4236030 (NASA/NSBRI 2014): urinary tract infections in space more common in women, treated with antibiotics; only women needed catheterisation

radiation.rule: Radiation limits come from the radiation document; this document does not redefine them (that document has no sex-specific value: 600 mSv career for everyone, NASA-STD-3001 2022).

coldStart.rule: No personal baseline (fewer than minSessions): absolute limits only, shown on screen; no sex-based relative reference.
